title: Fix ARM64 build: go mod download fails due to DNS timeout in container
description:
During arm64 container build, go mod download fails with DNS timeout when trying to reach proxy.golang.org.

## Error
```
RUN go mod download:
95.21 go: dario.cat/mergo@v1.0.2: Get "https://proxy.golang.org/...": dial tcp: lookup proxy.golang.org on 192.168.64.1:53: read udp 192.168.64.2:60471->192.168.64.1:53: i/o timeout
```

## Root Cause
apple/container ARM64 build containers cannot reach the internet via DNS (192.168.64.1 timeout).

## Fix
Vendor dependencies so the build requires no network access:
1. Run `go mod vendor` locally
2. Update Dockerfile.multiarch to COPY vendor/ directory
3. Add -mod=vendor to go build flags

title: Enable pushing multi-arch Docker images to GitHub Container Registry
description:
Enable pushing multi-architecture Docker images to GitHub Container Registry (ghcr.io).

## Requirements

1. Update Justfile with GitHub Container Registry recipes:
   - build-ghcr TAG - Build image for ghcr.io
   - push-ghcr TAG - Authenticate with GitHub and push multi-arch image to ghcr.io
   - Recipes should handle both AMD64 and ARM64

2. Configure GitHub authentication:
   - Use GITHUB_REGISTRY_TOKEN environment variable
   - Support authentication flow similar to goldenbraid project

3. Justfile configuration:
   - ghcr_image variable: ghcr.io/dictybase/modware-stock
   - Support custom tags (default: latest)

## Success Criteria

✓ build-ghcr recipe builds image for ghcr.io
✓ push-ghcr recipe authenticates and pushes both architectures
✓ Images are tagged correctly with namespace and tag
✓ GitHub authentication works with token-based login
✓ Recipes follow goldenbraid project patterns
close_reason: Added build-ghcr and push-ghcr recipes to justfile following goldenbraid patterns. Commit: 633263b

title: Implement multi-arch Docker builds
description:
Implement multi-architecture Docker image builds for modware-stock.

## Requirements

1. Create multi-arch Dockerfile (build/package/Dockerfile.multiarch):
   - Builder: golang:1.24-alpine with $BUILDPLATFORM
   - Runtime: gcr.io/distroless/static-debian12
   - Binary compression with upx (level 9)
   - Support TARGETOS, TARGETARCH build args

2. Create Justfile with recipes (following goldenbraid style):
   - build-multiarch     # Build both AMD64 and ARM64
   - build-amd64         # Build and load AMD64 locally
   - build-arm64         # Build and load ARM64 locally
   - test-amd64          # Build and test AMD64 (runs binary with --help)
   - test-arm64          # Build and test ARM64 via emulation (runs binary with --help)
   - setup-buildx        # Initialize Docker buildx
   - show-platforms      # Show available platforms
   - clean               # Remove built images

## Success Criteria

✓ Dockerfile builds successfully for both linux/amd64 and linux/arm64
✓ All Justfile recipes execute without errors
✓ test-amd64 and test-arm64 validate binary execution on both architectures
✓ Backward compatible (original Dockerfile untouched)
✓ No documentation files needed
close_reason: Implemented Dockerfile.multiarch and justfile with build/test recipes for both AMD64 and ARM64. No docs needed per user decision.

title: Add OS-aware container tool detection to justfile
description:
Update the justfile to detect the host OS and route container build/run commands to the appropriate tool:
- macOS (Apple silicon): use github.com/apple/container CLI
- Linux / other: use docker buildx (existing behavior)

## Plan

See: docs/plans/2026-02-20-os-aware-container-tool.md

## Quick Summary

1. Add OS detection variable using just's os() function:
   - on_macos := if os() == "macos" { "true" } else { "false" }

2. Refactor all recipes to use OS-aware commands:
   - build-amd64, build-arm64: container build --arch vs docker buildx build --platform
   - build-multiarch: container build --arch arm64 --arch amd64 vs docker buildx build --platform
   - test-amd64, test-arm64: container run --arch vs docker run --platform
   - setup-buildx: container system start vs docker buildx create
   - build-ghcr, push-ghcr: container registry login + container image push vs docker login + docker buildx --push

## Key Differences (macOS vs Linux)

| Operation      | macOS (container)                        | Linux (docker)                     |
|----------------|------------------------------------------|------------------------------------|
| Multi-arch     | --arch arm64 --arch amd64                | --platform linux/amd64,linux/arm64 |
| Push           | separate: container image push           | inline: --push flag                |
| Registry login | container registry login --password-stdin| docker login --password-stdin      |
| Buildx setup   | container system start                   | docker buildx create --use         |

## Success Criteria

✓ just --dry-run shows container commands on macOS
✓ just --dry-run shows docker commands on Linux
✓ All existing recipes preserved with same names
✓ No new files created
close_reason: All recipes refactored to use apple/container on macOS and docker buildx on Linux via on_macos variable. Commits: 334d6fd, 579e82a, 41144e4, fa94c1e, c80d0b7, 7104d04

comments.text:
# OS-Aware Container Tool Detection Implementation Plan

> **For Claude:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task.

**Goal:** Update the justfile to detect the host OS and route container commands to `apple/container` on macOS or `docker buildx` on Linux.

**Architecture:** Use just's built-in `os()` function to detect the platform at recipe-evaluation time. Define separate command variables for each tool, then use an `if` expression to select the right one. No new files needed — all changes are in the existing `justfile`.

**Tech Stack:** just 1.40+, apple/container CLI (`container`), Docker buildx

---

## Background

### apple/container vs docker buildx

| Concern | macOS (`container`) | Linux (`docker`) |
|---------|---------------------|------------------|
| Build | `container build --arch arm64 --arch amd64 -t img .` | `docker buildx build --platform linux/amd64,linux/arm64 -t img .` |
| Load single arch | `container build --arch amd64 --load -t img .` | `docker buildx build --platform linux/amd64 --load -t img .` |
| Run | `container run --rm img --help` | `docker run --rm img --help` |
| Run specific arch | `container run --arch amd64 --rm img --help` | `docker run --rm --platform linux/amd64 img --help` |
| Push | separate step: `container image push img` | inline `--push` flag |
| Registry login | `echo $TOKEN | container registry login --username user --password-stdin ghcr.io` | `echo $TOKEN | docker login ghcr.io -u user --password-stdin` |
| Buildx setup | not needed (native) | `docker buildx create --use` |

### just `os()` function

`os()` returns `"macos"`, `"linux"`, `"windows"`, etc.
Use it in variable assignments with `if`:

```justfile
tool := if os() == "macos" { "container" } else { "docker" }
```

---

## Task 1: Refactor variable section for OS detection

**Files:**
- Modify: `justfile`

**Step 1: Read the current justfile**

Run: `cat justfile`

Expected: Shows current variables and recipes.

**Step 2: Replace the variable section at the top**

```justfile
# Multi-Architecture Docker Build Justfile
# Recipes for building, testing, and pushing modware-stock images
# Automatically uses apple/container on macOS, docker buildx on Linux

# Variables
name        := "modware-stock"
namespace   := "dictybase"
dockerfile  := "build/package/Dockerfile.multiarch"
platforms   := "linux/amd64,linux/arm64"
github_user := "sba964"

image      := namespace + "/" + name
ghcr_image := "ghcr.io/" + image

# OS detection — routes to apple/container on macOS, docker on Linux
on_macos := if os() == "macos" { "true" } else { "false" }
```

**Step 3: Verify `just --evaluate` parses cleanly**

Run: `just --evaluate`

Expected: Shows all variables including `on_macos := "true"` (on macOS).

**Step 4: Commit**

```bash
git add justfile
git commit -m "refactor(justfile): add OS detection variable for container tool routing"
```

---

## Task 2: Refactor build-amd64 and build-arm64 recipes

**Files:**
- Modify: `justfile`

**Step 1: Replace `build-amd64` recipe**

```justfile
# Build and load AMD64 image locally for testing
build-amd64:
    @echo "Building {{image}} for linux/amd64 (local)..."
    {{ if on_macos == "true" { "container build --arch amd64 --load -t " + image + ":amd64 -f " + dockerfile + " ." } else { "docker buildx build --platform linux/amd64 --load -t " + image + ":amd64 -f " + dockerfile + " ." } }}
    @echo "✓ AMD64 image built and loaded"
```

**Step 2: Replace `build-arm64` recipe**

```justfile
# Build and load ARM64 image locally for testing
build-arm64:
    @echo "Building {{image}} for linux/arm64..."
    {{ if on_macos == "true" { "container build --arch arm64 --load -t " + image + ":arm64 -f " + dockerfile + " ." } else { "docker buildx build --platform linux/arm64 --load -t " + image + ":arm64 -f " + dockerfile + " ." } }}
    @echo "✓ ARM64 image built and loaded"
```

**Step 3: Verify syntax**

Run: `just --dry-run build-amd64`

Expected on macOS: Shows `container build --arch amd64 --load -t dictybase/modware-stock:amd64 ...`
Expected on Linux: Shows `docker buildx build --platform linux/amd64 --load ...`

**Step 4: Commit**

```bash
git add justfile
git commit -m "refactor(justfile): route build-amd64 and build-arm64 by OS"
```

---

## Task 3: Refactor build-multiarch recipe

**Files:**
- Modify: `justfile`

**Step 1: Replace `build-multiarch` recipe**

```justfile
# Build multi-architecture image (no push)
build-multiarch:
    @echo "Building {{image}} for amd64 and arm64..."
    {{ if on_macos == "true" { "container build --arch arm64 --arch amd64 -t " + image + ":multiarch -f " + dockerfile + " ." } else { "docker buildx build --platform " + platforms + " -t " + image + ":multiarch -f " + dockerfile + " ." } }}
    @echo "✓ Multi-architecture build completed"
```

**Step 2: Verify syntax**

Run: `just --dry-run build-multiarch`

Expected on macOS: Shows `container build --arch arm64 --arch amd64 ...`

**Step 3: Commit**

```bash
git add justfile
git commit -m "refactor(justfile): route build-multiarch by OS"
```

---

## Task 4: Refactor test-amd64 and test-arm64 recipes

**Files:**
- Modify: `justfile`

**Step 1: Replace `test-amd64` recipe**

```justfile
# Test the locally loaded AMD64 image
test-amd64: build-amd64
    @echo "Testing {{image}}:amd64..."
    {{ if on_macos == "true" { "container run --rm --arch amd64 " + image + ":amd64 --help" } else { "docker run --rm --platform linux/amd64 " + image + ":amd64 --help" } }}
    @echo "✓ AMD64 image test passed"
```

**Step 2: Replace `test-arm64` recipe**

```justfile
# Test the ARM64 image
test-arm64: build-arm64
    @echo "Testing {{image}}:arm64..."
    {{ if on_macos == "true" { "container run --rm --arch arm64 " + image + ":arm64 --help" } else { "docker run --rm --platform linux/arm64 " + image + ":arm64 --help" } }}
    @echo "✓ ARM64 image test passed"
```

**Step 3: Verify syntax**

Run: `just --dry-run test-amd64`

Expected on macOS: Shows `container run --rm --arch amd64 dictybase/modware-stock:amd64 --help`

**Step 4: Commit**

```bash
git add justfile
git commit -m "refactor(justfile): route test-amd64 and test-arm64 by OS"
```

---

## Task 5: Refactor setup-buildx and show-platforms recipes

**Files:**
- Modify: `justfile`

**Step 1: Replace `setup-buildx` recipe**

```justfile
# Setup container tool (buildx on Linux, container daemon on macOS)
setup-buildx:
    @echo "Setting up container tool..."
    {{ if on_macos == "true" { "container system start || true" } else { "docker buildx create --use || docker buildx use default" } }}
    {{ if on_macos == "true" { "container system status" } else { "docker buildx ls" } }}
```

**Step 2: Replace `show-platforms` recipe**

```justfile
# Show available platforms
show-platforms:
    {{ if on_macos == "true" { "container system property get build.rosetta && echo 'Platforms: linux/arm64 (native), linux/amd64 (Rosetta 2)'" } else { "docker buildx ls" } }}
```

**Step 3: Verify syntax**

Run: `just --dry-run setup-buildx`

Expected on macOS: Shows `container system start || true`

**Step 4: Commit**

```bash
git add justfile
git commit -m "refactor(justfile): route setup-buildx and show-platforms by OS"
```

---

## Task 6: Refactor build-ghcr and push-ghcr recipes

**Files:**
- Modify: `justfile`

On macOS, `apple/container` push is a separate step after build. On Linux, `docker buildx build --push` does it inline.

**Step 1: Replace `build-ghcr` recipe**

```justfile
# Build for GitHub Container Registry
build-ghcr tag="latest":
    @echo "Building {{ghcr_image}}:{{tag}} for amd64 and arm64..."
    {{ if on_macos == "true" { "container build --arch arm64 --arch amd64 -t " + ghcr_image + ":" + tag + " -f " + dockerfile + " ." } else { "docker buildx build --platform " + platforms + " -t " + ghcr_image + ":" + tag + " -f " + dockerfile + " ." } }}
    @echo "✓ GitHub Container Registry build completed"
```

**Step 2: Replace `push-ghcr` recipe**

```justfile
# Push to GitHub Container Registry
push-ghcr tag="latest":
    @echo "Logging into GitHub Container Registry..."
    {{ if on_macos == "true" { "echo $GITHUB_REGISTRY_TOKEN | container registry login --username " + github_user + " --password-stdin ghcr.io" } else { "echo $GITHUB_REGISTRY_TOKEN | docker login ghcr.io -u " + github_user + " --password-stdin" } }}
    @echo "Building {{ghcr_image}}:{{tag}}..."
    {{ if on_macos == "true" { "container build --arch arm64 --arch amd64 -t " + ghcr_image + ":" + tag + " -f " + dockerfile + " ." } else { "docker buildx build --platform " + platforms + " -t " + ghcr_image + ":" + tag + " -f " + dockerfile + " . --push" } }}
    {{ if on_macos == "true" { "container image push " + ghcr_image + ":" + tag } else { "" } }}
    @echo "✓ Successfully pushed to GitHub Container Registry"
```

**Step 3: Verify syntax**

Run: `just --dry-run push-ghcr`

Expected on macOS:
```
echo $GITHUB_REGISTRY_TOKEN | container registry login --username sba964 --password-stdin ghcr.io
container build --arch arm64 --arch amd64 -t ghcr.io/dictybase/modware-stock:latest -f build/package/Dockerfile.multiarch .
container image push ghcr.io/dictybase/modware-stock:latest
```

**Step 4: Commit**

```bash
git add justfile
git commit -m "refactor(justfile): route build-ghcr and push-ghcr by OS"
```

---

## Task 7: Final verification

**Step 1: List all recipes**

Run: `just --list`

Expected: All recipes visible with no syntax errors.

**Step 2: Dry-run all recipes on macOS**

```bash
just --dry-run build-multiarch
just --dry-run build-amd64
just --dry-run build-arm64
just --dry-run test-amd64
just --dry-run test-arm64
just --dry-run setup-buildx
just --dry-run show-platforms
just --dry-run build-ghcr
just --dry-run push-ghcr
just --dry-run push-ghcr v1.2.3
```

**Step 3: Verify `on_macos` evaluates correctly**

Run: `just --evaluate | grep on_macos`

Expected: `on_macos := "true"` on macOS

---

## Summary

**Deliverables:**
- Modified: `justfile` — all recipes now OS-aware

**Behavior:**
- macOS (Apple silicon): uses `container` CLI natively, Rosetta 2 for amd64
- Linux/CI: uses `docker buildx` (unchanged from current behavior)

**No files created or deleted.** Backward compatible for Linux CI.
